_meta.description: Document-rules config for plaint_injunction — suit for permanent injunction under S.38/39 SRA with Order 39 CPC temporary injunction application
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Three-fold test (prima facie / balance of convenience / irreparable injury) for interim is non-negotiable.

title: Plaint — Suit for Permanent Injunction (with Order 39 Application)

fields.label: Plaintiff full name
Plaintiff father's / husband's name
Plaintiff age
Plaintiff address
Defendant full name
Defendant address
Type of injunction sought
Legal right of plaintiff sought to be protected (proprietary / possessory / contractual / personal)
Subject-matter property / right description (schedule, boundaries if property)
Plaintiff's lawful possession / settled possession particulars
Title / possession documents (sale deed, lease, mutation, tax receipts)
Specific acts of interference / threatened interference by defendant (dates, nature)
Nature of irreparable injury — incapable of compensation in money
Balance of convenience in favour of plaintiff
Prima facie case statement
Temporary injunction under Order 39 R.1-2 CPC sought
Specific interim orders sought (status quo / restraint / preservation)
Confirm no bar under S.41 SRA applies (e.g., injunction not against judicial proceedings, public office, etc.)
Cause of action — when threat / interference first manifested
Limitation — Art. 113 (residuary, 3 years) or specific article
Territorial jurisdiction (S.16 CPC for property, S.20 otherwise)
Court fee paid (Rs.) — usually fixed for injunction (state Schedule)
Suit valuation
Advocate name
Bar Council enrollment number

mandatory_clauses.name: Legal Right Protected — S.38 SRA
mandatory_clauses.description: S.38(3) — perpetual injunction may be granted to prevent breach of obligation existing in favour of plaintiff

mandatory_clauses.name: Threatened or Actual Interference
mandatory_clauses.description: Specific acts of defendant constituting threat or breach

mandatory_clauses.name: Prima Facie Case
mandatory_clauses.description: Statement of triable issue with serious question to be decided

mandatory_clauses.name: Irreparable Injury
mandatory_clauses.description: Injury not adequately compensable in damages

mandatory_clauses.name: S.41 SRA — No Statutory Bar
mandatory_clauses.description: Confirm injunction not barred under S.41(a)-(j)

mandatory_clauses.name: Prayer
mandatory_clauses.description: Permanent injunction + costs + interim relief in separate application

mandatory_clauses.name: Affidavit in support
mandatory_clauses.description: Order VI R.15(4) + Order 39 R.3 for interim

verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {plaintiff_name}, son/daughter/wife of {plaintiff_father_name}, aged about {plaintiff_age} years, resident of {plaintiff_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above plaint are true and correct to my personal knowledge, and matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Plaintiff

promptInstructions: Draft a plaint for permanent injunction under Sections 38 and/or 39 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963.
S.38 SRA — perpetual prohibitory injunction granted to prevent breach of obligation existing in favour of plaintiff (express or implied).
S.39 SRA — perpetual mandatory injunction granted to compel performance of certain acts where breach has occurred.
S.40 SRA — damages may be claimed in addition to or in substitution.

S.41 SRA — situations where injunction CANNOT be granted: (a) to restrain person from prosecuting judicial proceedings; (b) to restrain person from filing in superior court; (c) to restrain government from legislative function; (d) to restrain criminal proceedings; (e) to prevent breach of contract that cannot be specifically enforced; (f) to prevent continuing breach where plaintiff has acquiesced; (g) where damages adequate; (h) when conduct of plaintiff disentitles him; (i) when plaintiff has no personal interest; (j) to prevent removal from public office.
S.42 SRA — special provision: injunction to enforce negative agreement.
Para 1-2: Parties description.
Para 3: Plaintiff's legal right / interest — proprietary, possessory, contractual.
Para 4: Plaintiff's actual or settled possession (for property suits — possession is sufficient against world except true owner).
Para 5: Documents establishing title / possession.
Para 6: Defendant's specific acts of interference, threats, attempted dispossession — with dates.
Para 7: Why damages are inadequate — irreparable injury (e.g., property has special value, loss of goodwill, continuing trespass).
Para 8: Balance of convenience — comparative hardship analysis.
Para 9: Confirm no statutory bar under S.41 SRA applies.
Para 10: Cause of action.
Para 11: Limitation — Article 113 residuary (3 years from when right to sue accrues).
Para 12: Territorial jurisdiction — S.16 CPC for immovable property suits.
Para 13: Court fee and valuation — typically fixed court fee on injunction in state Schedules (e.g., Bihar Court Fees / UP Court Fees Act); refer state-specific notification.
ALWAYS file a separate application under Order 39 R.1-2 CPC for temporary injunction with supporting affidavit (Order 39 R.3).

Interim injunction tripod test (Dalpat Kumar v. Prahlad Singh; M. Gurudas v. Rasaranjan): (i) prima facie case — serious question to be tried; (ii) balance of convenience in favour of plaintiff; (iii) irreparable injury if injunction refused.
Where ex parte ad-interim sought: Order 39 R.3 proviso — court must record reasons for ex parte order, plaintiff must file undertaking and deliver copy to defendant within prescribed time.
Where status quo claimed — distinguish from injunction; status quo presumes existing factual matrix preserved.
Verification and affidavit mandatory.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Preventive relief — temporary or perpetual injunction
Damages in lieu of or in addition to injunction
Cases in which temporary injunction may be granted
Injunction to restrain breach of contract or other injury
Notice before grant of injunction; ex parte conditions
Order of injunction may be discharged, varied or set aside
Residuary — 3 years from when right to sue accrues
Rights and liabilities of seller and buyer

filing_checklist: Application under Order 39 R.1-2 CPC for temporary injunction with affidavit (Order 39 R.3)
Application under Order 39 R.3 proviso for ex parte ad-interim injunction (if applicable) with reasons
Affidavit in support of plaint (Order VI R.15(4))
Tax receipts, electricity bills evidencing possession
Photographs / videos of property and acts of interference
Notice issued to defendant (if any) and reply
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: plaintiff_name and defendant_name must not be empty
section_41_sra_bars must be true (i.e., no bar)
If interim_injunction_sought=true, separate Order 39 application must be filed
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
key_citations: Dalpat Kumar v. Prahlad Singh (1992) 1 SCC 719 — Triple test for temporary injunction
M. Gurudas v. Rasaranjan (2006) 8 SCC 367 — Reiteration of triple test
Maria Margarida Sequeria Fernandes v. Erasmo Jack de Sequeria (2012) 5 SCC 370 — Possession suits and burden
Anathula Sudhakar v. P. Buchi Reddy (2008) 4 SCC 594 — Suit for injunction simpliciter — possession is sufficient against world except true owner
Premji Ratansey Shah v. Union of India (1994) 5 SCC 547 — Injunction not to issue in favour of trespassers against true owner
Best Sellers Retail (India) Pvt Ltd v. Aditya Birla Nuvo Ltd (2012) 6 SCC 792 — Three-fold test for interim injunction in commercial matters
